data.title: Fanatics names Afterpay as preferred BNPL partner
data.description:
Sports apparel and merchandise retailer Fanatics has named Afterpay as its preferred partner for buy now, pay later (BNPL) payments processing.

The move means that shoppers across Fanatics’ ecommerce sites can now use Afterpay’s “Pay in 4” and “Pay Monthly” offerings. Pay in 4 allows consumers to make their purchases and then complete their payments in four installments over six weeks, without interest. Meanwhile, Pay Monthly allows consumers to complete payments over 24 months for purchases from $100 to $20,000.

Fanatics websites include:

  • Fanatics.com
  • Lids.com
  • NBAStore.com
  • NHLShop.com
  • Other associated partner sites

Fanatics is No. 13 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

Fanatics is also No. 132 in Digital Commerce 360’s new AI Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Why Fanatics is working with Afterpay on BNPL

“Afterpay gives our customers the flexibility today’s shoppers expect, so fans can support their teams and celebrate the biggest moments in sports,” said Tucker Kain, chief strategy and growth officer at Fanatics, in a statement. “This feature allows us to further our mission to relentlessly enhance the fan experience, whether that’s through the personalized discovery Fanatics Ads brings to shopping, the live energy of Fanatics Fest, or the flexibility Afterpay offers at checkout, and make our world-class assortment of products available and accessible in more ways than ever before.”

The retailer and Afterpay had already established a relationship that included partnering for Fanatics Fest in summer 2026. Fanatics Fest is a multi-day sports, collecting and cultural festival. In 2026, Fanatics held it at the Javits Center in New York City.

“Being selected as Fanatics’ preferred BNPL partner is a meaningful milestone for Afterpay as we continue expanding into high-intent shopping categories where flexibility matters,” said Tanuj Parikh, head of revenue for Cash App and Afterpay. “Fanatics sits at the center of sports culture, bringing fans closer to the teams and athletes they love. Together, we’re offering fans more flexible options at checkout while supporting one of the most dynamic commerce ecosystems in sports.”

Block, Inc. (formerly Square, Inc.) fully owns Afterpay. It also owns:

  • Bitkey
  • Buzz
  • Cash App
  • Proto
  • Square
  • Tidal
  • Weebly

Afterpay framed the partnership as underscoring its “continued momentum with leading retail, fashion, lifestyle, and commerce brands as more merchants look to meet customer demand for flexible payment options.”

It added that fans can expect to see Afterpay and Fanatics partner in more ways going forward.

data.title: Costco launches nationwide on DoorDash
data.description:
Costco saved a place for DoorDash in its plans to expand delivery options in the U.S., opening up options for orders through the same-day, last-mile platform.

DoorDash’s announcement represented a significant expansion of its relationship with Costco, which already included service in Australia, New Zealand, Sweden, Iceland and Puerto Rico. It also arrived on Sept. 17 in the same week that saw Costco and Uber Eats roll out new ordering options in the U.S.

Costco is No. 7 in the Top 2000 Database. The database is Digital Commerce 360’s ranking of the largest online retailers in North America by their annual ecommerce sales. It’s also the fourth-largest Mass Merchant in the database.

Why Costco is important for DoorDash

“Costco members have been asking for Costco on DoorDash, and today we’re delivering,” said Mike Goldblatt, vice president of enterprise partnerships at DoorDash. “By pairing Costco’s quality, value and selection with DoorDash’s reach and local delivery network, we’re giving members more flexibility in how they shop.”

In addition to demand from Costco members, DoorDash also saw interest among users on its own platform, where it shared that “Costco ranked among the most-searched retailers not yet available on DoorDash.”

Moving forward, DoorDash will provide Costco members with the ability to order groceries, pantry staples, household essentials, electronics, seasonal merchandise, Kirkland Signature products and other products from local Costco warehouse locations. Those orders will be available for same-day delivery.

“The U.S. launch also marks the next chapter in a global partnership already serving Costco members around the world,” Goldblatt stated.

How Costco members will be able to use DoorDash

More than 4,000 products will be available from Costco through DoorDash, according to the vendor’s announcement. To order, U.S.-based Costco members will be able to search for the retailer in the DoorDash app and enter their Costco membership information to complete their transactions.

In cases where a DoorDash user is not already a Costco member, they will be presented with information to sign up.

Costco CEO Ron Vachris told investors during a May earnings call that same-day delivery from third-party partners had “become a highly effective way to deliver more convenience” to members. Costco works with Instacart, in addition to Uber Eats and DoorDash.

In the meantime, delivery has been an important part of the growing online grocery market, where sales increased by at least 20% year over year in the six consecutive quarters through Q1 2026, according to analysis by the firm Brick Meets Click.

data.title: Online marketplaces and tech lift August Ecommerce Stock Index results
data.description:
New results are in from August activity in the Baird/Digital Commerce 360 Ecommerce Stock Index. The month saw positive results for both Online Marketplaces and Ecommerce Technology, despite dips for Online Retail and International firms.

Wix and Shopify posted August’s biggest gains, while Amazon, Bed Bath & Beyond and JD dropped.

August takeaways from the Baird/Digital Commerce 360 Ecommerce Stock Index

  • The Baird/Digital Commerce 360 Ecommerce Stock Index was up 3.5% in August, as Online Marketplaces outperformed other categories.
  • Wix (+60%), Shopify (+26%) and Airbnb (+21%) recorded the month’s highest percentage gains.
  • International companies lagged behind the rest of the index, falling by 3.4%.

This index is a collaboration between Digital Commerce 360 and the financial advisory, capital markets, asset management and private equity firm Baird. It intends to provide perspective into how public markets value companies and technology providers that power digital commerce. The index contains four categories capturing activity extending throughout the Americas and China:

  1. Online Marketplaces
  2. Online Retail
  3. Ecommerce Technology
  4. International Companies

Readers should note that this index complements insights from Digital Commerce 360’s Top 2000 Database. The market research tool specifically tracks North American online retailers and their web sales.

The Baird/Digital Commerce 360 Ecommerce Stock Index, meanwhile, covers both B2C retail and B2B ecommerce companies, in addition to the technology vendors that serve them, with a broader focus on global activity. All commentary and reporting is provided for informational purposes only and is not intended to be financial advice.

Click here to read July’s ecommerce stock index results.

August ecommerce stock index results

“The Baird/Digital Commerce Ecommerce Stock Index increased nearly 3.5% during August, another positive performance after the 9% increase in July, and once again outperforming the broader S&P index, which was up 2.6% for the month,” said Colin Sebastian, Baird’s managing director and senior research analyst covering internet/ecommerce.

In a shift from earlier summer months, Ecommerce Technology companies tracked in the index saw gains in August from their July close. However, Online Marketplaces saw the strongest growth.

“Notably, there was clear divergence by subcategory, with healthy performance for Marketplaces and Ecommerce Technology stocks, while Online Retail and International sectors were slightly lower for the month,” Sebastian added.

Among the companies recording the index’s best results in August were the ecommerce site platform Wix, followed by Shopify.

“Strongest individual Ecommerce stocks last month included Wix (+60%) and Shopify (+26%) both benefiting from recovering valuations for software stocks as the AI trade took a breather; Airbnb (+21%) as the company continues to build out a broader marketplace platform for travel services, and DoorDash and Carvana were both up 18% as consumer trends remained healthy,” Sebastian assessed.

Shopify revenue and gross merchandise volume (GMV) both grew year over year in the platform provider’s most recent fiscal Q2, which ended June 30. That quarter was not only the 13th in a row that Shopify increased its revenue by more than 25% year over year. It also marked the fifth consecutive quarter in which Shopify GMV was up by more than 30%.

Online Retail as a category was down by 0.6% at the end of August, as Amazon shares alone fell 4%. Still, Sebastian noted optimism looking ahead to the end of the year.

“Our checks suggest ongoing healthy ecommerce trends, and we expect solid Q4 ‘Holiday period’ online spending trends, with potential upside to our initial 6% year-over-year industry growth forecast for 2026,” he stated.

data.title: Lowe's launches drone delivery in partnership with Wing, DoorDash
data.description:
Lowe’s said it has become the first home improvement retailer to offer drone delivery for online orders, working with Alphabet’s Wing and DoorDash on deliveries.

The newest fulfillment method delivers select home improvement products directly to Lowe’s DIY and Pro customers in as fast as 20 minutes, the retailer said. Its drone delivery pilot is now live at Lowe’s store in Matthews, North Carolina, and it adds to the retailer’s same-day fulfillment options. The other options include buy online, pick up in store (BOPIS), curbside pickup and same-day delivery.

Lowe’s is No. 9 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

Lowe’s is also No. 90 in Digital Commerce 360’s new AI Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Products eligible for Lowe’s drone delivery

Lowe’s is offering drone delivery in partnership with Wing and DoorDash. Consumers can order Lowe’s products for delivery through the DoorDash app, which Wing drones will then deliver.

The retailer said its initial pilot is limited to “a curated list of eligible products.” The pilot program includes more than 100 SKUs. Those include:

  • All-purpose cleaner
  • Caulk
  • Hand tools
  • Household batteries
  • Paint products such as painter’s tape
  • Screwdrivers
  • Soap

Lowe’s said it’s testing its last-mile fulfillment by using its physical stores as hubs for staging drone dispatch areas. That process integrates DoorDash’s third-party marketplace demand into specialized drone delivery, the retailer said.

Lowe’s said the drone delivery pilot builds on its broader efforts to use technology to remove friction from home improvement. It noted Mylow, Lowe’s AI assistant for customers, and Mylow Companion, its AI-powered assistant for store associates, as recent innovations. Together, the two assistants have helped answer more than 25 million questions since launching in 2025, according to Lowe’s.

“Home improvement is an inherently friction-filled experience,” said Seemantini Godbole, chief information and AI officer at Lowe’s. “Any technology we implement is designed to eliminate that friction so our customers can complete their projects quickly. By piloting drone delivery, we’re addressing a real project pain point with an innovative solution that is integrated into the retail journey, giving our hometown customers next-generation fulfillment right when they need it.”

data.title: JD Sports deploys Algolia for agentic commerce strategy
data.description:
JD Sports has deployed Algolia as the retailer’s governing intelligence layer on which to build its agentic commerce strategy.

Announced Sept. 22, the companies seek to enable product discovery and shopping through agentic artificial intelligence (AI) platforms. JD Sports initially implemented Algolia into its tech stack in 2024.

Since then, JD Sports said:

  • Revenue from search has increased 22%.
  • Search click-through rates have increased 7.65%.
  • Product listing page (PLP) click-through rates have increased 73%.
  • PLP revenue has increased 16%.

JD Sports is No. 28 in the Europe Database. The market research tool tracks the region’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

The retailer said it operates more than 4,800 stores globally. It also has more than 9 million active loyalty program members.

Algolia said it primes JD Sports’ catalog so AI agents can find the answers they need for “conversational, intent-heavy queries.” Still, it uses the same catalog and ranking logic that powers JD Sports’ website.

JD Sports said as its ecommerce operations and product catalogs expanded, merchandising teams were spending “significant time manually tuning results, boosting products and maintaining static rules.” That model could not keep up with shifting trends, seasonality and shopper behavior, according to the companies.

JD Sports, working with Algolia Professional Services, moved its website to a MACH ecommerce architecture. MACH is an acronym referring to four technology principles:

  1. Microservices. This refers to individual, small features that run as independent services rather than part of one large codebase.
  2. API-first. Features communicate through application programming interfaces (APIs). That enables merchants to plug in third-party tools.
  3. Cloud-native. The site fully runs on the cloud.
  4. Headless. The front end is separate from the back end.

“Replacing a highly manual search and merchandising process with an AI-native foundation changed how we operate…,” said Kristin Matter, vice president of digital operations at JD Sports. “We respond faster to changing shopper behavior and emerging trends, our merchandisers spend their time on strategy instead of tuning, and the revenue gains follow.”

How JD Sports is optimizing for agentic commerce

JD Sports now uses dynamic re-ranking (DRR). That means it uses real-time click and conversion signals to identify trending products and automatically adjust their placement, the companies explained. It does so within merchandising rules that JD Sports’ team defines. The retailer can see and reverse each adjustment.

The retailer saw a 2.2% increase in click-through rate from DRR. Additionally, DRR led to a 4% increase in JD Sports’ add-to-cart rate as well as 4% growth in its conversion rate.

JD Sports and Algolia said they’ve begun using AI “to proactively surface” emerging search trends, inventory shifts and merchandising opportunities. They also have been using it “to tailor discovery to individual shopper intent.”

The same process that displays search results now works for AI agents, the companies explained. That gives JD Sports a way to “control relevance” across shopping channels.

“JD Sports understood before most that discovery is a growth engine, not a website feature, and a 22% lift in search revenue is a P&L result, not an IT metric,” said Stephen Lynch, CEO at Algolia.

Lynch said in a category where demand shifts weekly, “winning takes intelligence merchandisers can inspect and control, not a black box they’re asked to trust.”

He added that he sees the next wave of retail growth going to the companies whose catalogs agents can shop. To enable that, retailers have to make their catalogs structured, current and accurate, he said.
